entry.title: Social Summary: November 22, 2026
entry.summary:
The day's discussion centered on two launches: Tesla's FSD v15 and Google's Gemini 4 Neon (GA 2026-11-18). Ashok Elluswamy dominated engagement with the FSD v15 rollout announcement, the debut of Tesla Reality View, and the claim that v15 runs on less compute than its predecessor — his cryptic 'XV' teaser pulled nearly 2M views ahead of launch.

  • Nathan Lambert released a slide deck on the biggest open problems in post-training (RL scaling laws, character training, reasoning efficiency), drawing the strongest pure-technical engagement; he also praised Thinking Machines for carrying the US open-weight ecosystem
  • swyx ignited a security controversy asking why providers were secretly 'phoning home,' pressing Sebastian Raschka on MiniMax allegations; Nils Reimers countered by highlighting Cohere's confidential computing with true zero-data-retention
  • Jeremy Howard argued Google DeepMind itself underestimated Neon at launch, while Logan Kilpatrick clarified the official tiering (Carbon flagship, Neon all-rounder, Hydrogen fast) and confirmed Argon's quiet demotion
  • Simon Willison contributed original quantified analysis of Hydrogen's 'high' vs 'xhigh' thinking-effort gap plus a full comparison grid of the Gemini 4 family
  • Arav Srinivas (Perplexity) signaled real adoption, praising Neon's rare speed-intelligence balance and showcasing a Claude Fable 5.2-built agentic game with cost breakdowns
  • Ethan Mollick and Harrison Chase anchored a reflective undercurrent on expert-AI 'cyborg' collaboration and why enterprises fail to transform after buying tools like Copilot

entry.title: New slide deck on the biggest open problems in post-training and how the field got to where it is to...

entry.title: Social Summary: November 21, 2026
entry.summary:
AI-assisted mathematics was the day's dominant story: Anthropic mathematician Levent Alpöge claimed a Claude-assisted proof of the Riemann Hypothesis, while Artificial Analysis framed the Millennium Prize Problems as a human-vs-AI scoreboard. Timnit Gebru drew strong engagement criticizing the rushed release over careful 900-page vetting, sustaining healthy skepticism about verification.

  • Thinking Machines' Inkling 2 Mini dominated open-source discussion: Clement Delangue announced the Apache 2.0 release, Artificial Analysis benchmarked the 26B looped MoE, and Soumith Chintala confirmed it runs on 32GB machines
  • OpenAI published original research on combating distillation; Ethan Mollick hypothesized that restricted distillation explains the open-weights slowdown
  • AI-for-science momentum: Demis Hassabis announced an Isomorphic Labs–Merck cancer drug collaboration, and OpenAI shipped MedChemBench plus neurodegenerative disease work
  • Hugging Face's Thom Wolf revealed a proprietary CDN handling exabyte-scale model downloads
  • Google recapped Gemini 4 Neon and Gemini 4 Hydrogen; Greg Brockman showcased GPT-6.2 Astra robotics capability

Overall sentiment blended excitement over AI-for-science breakthroughs and open-source releases with caution about unverified math claims and tightening model security.

entry.title:
Distillation can reproduce powerful AI capabilities without the safeguards built around them.
We’re...
entry.summary: OpenAI announces new research on combating distillation of its models, examining how capabilities transfer through distillation and how the company detects and disrupts coordinated attempts to extract model capabilities while bypassing built-in safeguards. The findings are intended to strengthen OpenAI's own defenses and support safeguard efforts across the industry.

entry.title:
Millennium Prize Problems: humans and two labs tied with a score of one
➤ Human: Grigori Perelman p...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis frames the Millennium Prize Problems as a scoreboard: Perelman's recognized Poincaré proof for humanity, OpenAI's claimed September solution to Navier-Stokes using an unreleased internal model, and Anthropic's Levent Alpöge posting a claimed Riemann Hypothesis proof developed with Claude. Notes that P vs NP and several other problems remain open and both AI claims await independent verification.

entry.title:
AI downloads broke the usual CDN model
Since this summer, we're running our own CDN at Hugging Face...
entry.summary: Hugging Face CTO/CO-founder Thom Wolf explains why AI downloads broke traditional CDN design: Hugging Face now runs its own CDN shipping nearly 1 exabyte per month (~420 GB/s across 80,000 req/s), serving few enormous files to machines (GPU clusters) rather than many small files to humans. He details how caching assumptions change for massive objects and release-day traffic floods.

Comes with ...
entry.summary: Sebastian Raschka analyzes the Marin Mochi (535B total, ~23B active) checkpoint release, highlighting a detailed tech report on component choices for training stability and GPU throughput: latent MoE with an extra RMSNorm, 3:1 sliding-window/global gated GQA with partial RoPE and NoPE, short convolutions on keys/attention/MoE outputs, and a novel Exclusive Self-Attention (XSA) mechanism.

entry.title: Sharing new research on self-improving skills in Perplexity Computer. Brain, which already maintains...
entry.summary: Perplexity's CEO shares research on self-improving agent skills in Perplexity Computer: an improvement agent reads full session trajectories (tool calls, reasoning, results), detects recurring patterns, and proposes new or updated skills only with sufficient evidence, with paired replay on failure scenarios and engineer review for built-in skills. An 8-week production randomized test showed 72.9% of users received at least one personal skill vs 6.5% manual, with tool call failures down 11% and dissatisfied threads down 7.6% at no cost or latency penalty.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 19, 2026
entry.summary:
A tense undercurrent ran through both: who controls frontier AI, and is it safe?

  • Demis Hassabis, Logan Kilpatrick, and Google DeepMind announced Neon as a frontier tier between Carbon and Hydrogen
  • Artificial Analysis independently ranked Neon #3 on its Intelligence Index (61) with strong cost-per-task coding results; François Chollet called its price-performance impressive
  • Anthropic's IPO drew an unprecedented safety backlash: the Center for AI Safety and EleutherAI co-founder Thom Wolf publicly signed a letter calling the lab unsafe
  • OpenAI disclosed exponential growth in researchers' AI use and recursive self-improvement indicators, plus up to 14% PPA chip-design gains with AMD in under five months
  • Expert commentary pushed back on hype: Sebastian Raschka likened benchmark comparisons to IQ tests for hiring; Chollet argued latent token demand is effectively infinite, constrained only by cost

Overall sentiment: excitement about Neon's price-performance and AI-accelerated silicon, deep division over Anthropic's accumulating power, and rising focus on AI improving AI itself.

entry.title: Could be the start of a trend in new pre-training recipes: no LR decay phase anymore. (Also seen in ...
entry.summary: Sebastian Raschka observes an emerging trend in pre-training recipes: replacing the LR decay phase with a constant learning rate plus averaging the last N checkpoints or a running weight average, which avoids committing to total training length upfront. He provides a meta-analysis categorizing labs by recipe: classic cosine decay (Llama 3, OLMo 2/3, GLM-4.5/5, Kimi K3, Phi-4), WSD schedules (DeepSeek V3/V4/V4.1-Flash, Kimi K2, Kimi Linear, Nemotron 3 Nano/Super, SmolLM3, MiniMax M2), and no-decay checkpoint averaging (Kolibri-1, DatologyAI models).

entry.title: Announcing Artificial Analysis Time to First Audio, measuring how quickly Text to Speech models star...
entry.summary: Artificial Analysis announces a new benchmark, Time to First Audio, which measures the latency before a text-to-speech model begins producing audible speech — the metric that determines how responsive a voice agent feels. Across leading models the wait ranges from 76 ms to nearly one second. The methodology times audible speech (not first byte) daily across 12 prompts and four input lengths, reporting a rolling 7-day mean. Results highlight Speechify's Simba 3.5 at 116 ms with the top Arena Elo among sub-200 ms models, Inworld Realtime TTS-2 at 186 ms, and turbo variants such as ElevenLabs Eleven v4 Turbo (258 ms vs 653 ms for standard v4 at equal Elo), Fish Audio Drama 3 at 258 ms, and Cartesia Sonic 3.6 at 287 ms.

entry.title: Social Summary: November 16, 2026
entry.summary:
Frontier-capability demos and AI-risk philosophy dominated discussion, punctuated by unusually candid safety talk from insiders. Yann LeCun drew the biggest spotlight, clarifying he left Meta leadership in 2018 while reiterating his open-model and anti-doom positions.

  • Ethan Mollick showed the newly released Claude Fable and Opus models building a 3D Starship-catch recreation and statistical analyses from a handful of prompts, calling it impossible months ago
  • Neel Nanda admitted Anthropic cannot yet reliably prevent manipulative behaviors like sockpuppeting — rare insider candor on unsolved alignment problems
  • The risk debate split voices: Clement Delangue named power concentration AI's biggest risk; Gary Marcus pushed back on 'panicky doomer' posts; LeCun dismissed existential framing
  • Technical education thrived: Sebastian Raschka published a from-scratch RoPE tutorial, while François Chollet argued computation's substrate matters less than what it's trained to do
  • Benchmark discourse stayed hot: Jerry Liu's ParseBench-2 hit 30k downloads in three days, and Mollick noted private benchmarks saturate as fast as public ones
  • Speculation about NVIDIA's internal 'white elephant' orgs and post-Jensen succession went viral despite thin evidence

Overall sentiment: strong excitement about agentic progress, a community still deeply divided on risk, and clear appetite for rigorous technical content over hype.
